arxiv-2011-05430.title: Entropy Admissibility of the Limit Solution for a Nonlocal Model of Traffic Flow
arxiv-2011-05430.creator: Alberto Bressan, Wen Shen
arxiv-2011-05430.description: Abstract We consider a conservation law model of traffic flow, where the velocity of each car depends on a weighted average of the traffic density ρ \rho ahead. The averaging kernel is of exponential type: w ε ( s ) = ε − 1 e − s / ε w_{\varepsilon}(s)=\varepsilon^{-1}e^{-s/\varepsilon} .

arxiv-2303-12090.title: Relativistic Polytropic Models of Charged Anisotropic Compact Object
arxiv-2303-12090.creator: H. Nazar, M. Azam, G. Abbas, Riaz Ahmed, R. Naeem
arxiv-2303-12090.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by H. Nazar, M. Azam, G. Abbas, Riaz Ahmed, R. Naeem. In this paper, we have introduced new viable solutions of Einstein-Maxwell field equations by incorporating the features of anisotropic matter distribution in the realm of General theory of Relativity ( G ​ R GR ). For this procurement, we have employed a Finch-Skea spacetime along with a generalized polytropic equation of state ( E ​ o ​ S EoS ).

arxiv-2311-13966.title: Testing Continuous Spontaneous Localization model with charged macro-molecules
arxiv-2311-13966.creator: Emil Lenler-Eriksen, Michael Drewsen, Matteo Carlesso
arxiv-2311-13966.description: Abstract In the last decade, a growing interest has been devoted to models of spontaneous collapse of the wavefunction, known also as collapse models. They coherently solve the well-known quantum measurement problem by suitably modifying the Schrödinger evolution. Quantum experiments are now finally within the reach of testing such models (and thus testing the limits of quantum theory).

arxiv-2401-01684.title: Post-hoc Evaluation of Nodes Influence in Information Cascades: The Case of Coordinated Accounts CCS: Networks Network algorithms CCS: Applied computing CCS: Mathematics of computing Trees CCS: Mathematics of computing Graph algorithms
arxiv-2401-01684.creator: Niccolò Di Marco, Sara Brunetti, Matteo Cinelli, Walter Quattrociocchi
arxiv-2401-01684.description: Abstract . In the last years, social media has gained an unprecedented amount of attention, playing a pivotal role in shaping the contemporary landscape of communication and connection. However, Coordinated Inhautentic Behaviour (CIB), defined as orchestrated efforts by entities to deceive or mislead users about their identity and intentions, has emerged as a tactic to exploit the online discourse.

arxiv-2502-12040.title: Inferring contact network characteristics from epidemic data via compact mean-field models
arxiv-2502-12040.creator: Andrés Guzmán 1 , Federico Malizia 1 , Gyeong Ho Park 2 , Boseung Choi 2,3,4 , Diana Cole 5 , István Z. Kiss 1,6
arxiv-2502-12040.description: Abstract Modelling epidemics using contact networks provides a significant improvement over classical compartmental models by explicitly incorporating the network of contacts. However, while network-based models describe disease spread on a given contact structure, their potential for inferring the underlying network from epidemic data remains largely unexplored.

arxiv-2504-11274.title: Isomeric yield ratios and mass spectrometry of Y and Nb isotopes in the neutron-rich N=60 region: the unusual case of 98 Y Journal: Physics Letters B
arxiv-2504-11274.creator: Simone Cannarozzo, Stephan Pomp, Anu Kankainen, Iain Moore, Marek Stryjczyk, Ali Al-Adili, Andreas Solders, Ville Virtanen, Tommi Eronen, Zhihao Gao, Zhuang Ge, Arthur Jaries, Mattias Lantz, Maxime Mougeot, Heikki Penttilä, Andrea Raggio, Jouni Ruotsalainen
arxiv-2504-11274.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Simone Cannarozzo, Stephan Pomp, Anu Kankainen, Iain Moore, Marek Stryjczyk, Ali Al-Adili, Andreas Solders, Ville Virtanen, Tommi Eronen, Zhihao Gao, Zhuang Ge, Arthur Jaries, Mattias Lantz, Maxime Mougeot, Heikki Penttilä, Andrea Raggio, Jouni Ruotsalainen. The isomeric yield ratio (IYR) of fission products is an observable that carries relevant information about the fragments emerging from the scission of a fissioning nucleus.

arxiv-2506-11108.title: History-Aware Cross-Attention Reinforcement: Self-Supervised Multi-Turn and Chain-of-Thought Fine-Tuning with vLLM
arxiv-2506-11108.creator: Andrew Kiruluta, Andreas Lemos, Priscilla Burity
arxiv-2506-11108.description: Abstract We present CAGSR–vLLM–MTC, an extension of our Self-Supervised Cross-Attention–Guided Reinforcement (CAGSR) framework, now implemented on the high-performance vLLM runtime, to address both multi-turn dialogue and chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning. Building upon our original single-turn approach, we first instrumented vLLM ’s C++/CUDA kernels to asynchronously capture per layer, per head cross-attention weights during generation.

arxiv-2511-23475.title: AnyTalker: Scaling Multi-Person Talking Video Generation with Interactivity Refinement
arxiv-2511-23475.creator: Zhizhou Zhong, Yicheng Ji, Zhe Kong, Yiying Liu, Jiarui Wang, Jiasun Feng, Lupeng Liu, Xiangyi Wang, Yanjia Li, Yuqing She Ying Qin, Huan Li, Shuiyang Mao, Wei Liu, Wenhan Luo
arxiv-2511-23475.description: Abstract Recently, multi-person video generation has started to gain prominence. While a few preliminary works have explored audio-driven multi-person talking video generation, they often face challenges due to the high costs of diverse multi-person data collection and the difficulty of driving multiple identities with coherent interactivity.

arxiv-2602-03823.title: Preference-based Conditional Treatment Effects and Policy Learning
arxiv-2602-03823.creator: Dovid Parnas, Mathieu Even, Julie Josse, Uri Shalit
arxiv-2602-03823.description: Abstract We introduce a new preference-based framework for conditional treatment effect estimation and policy learning, built on the Conditional Preference-based Treatment Effect (CPTE). CPTE requires only that outcomes be ranked under a preference rule, unlocking flexible modeling of heterogeneous effects with multivariate, ordinal, or preference-driven outcomes.

pmc-10824239.title: Chlorophyll a fluorescence as a tool to monitor physiological status in the leaves of Artemisia ordosica under root cutting conditions
pmc-10824239.creator: Ying Liu, Chuangang Gong, Weihao Pei, Kaixuan Fan, Wenjing Shen
pmc-10824239.description: BackgroundRoot cutting caused by underground coal mining subsidence is among the leading causes of plant damage in western China. Detection of root cutting stress is of great importance in evaluating the degree of plant damage and changes in physiological conditions in underground coal mining disturbance conditions.

pmc-11462180.title: The high-value and sustainable utilization of grape pomace: A review
pmc-11462180.creator: Changsen Wang, Yilin You, Weidong Huang, Jicheng Zhan
pmc-11462180.description: A large portion of global grape production has been utilized for wine production, accompanied by tremendous pressure to dispose grape pomace. To achieve circular economy, the high-value recycling of grape pomace must be considered. The social level barriers to circular economy promotion are also important constraints, like the acceptability of upcycled products.

pmc-11533336.title: Left atrial function during exercise stress echocardiography as a sign of paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation
pmc-11533336.creator: Angela Zagatina, Quirino Ciampi, Jesus Vazquez Peteiro, Elena Kalinina, Irina Begidova, Ratnasari Padang, Alla Boshchenko, Elisa Merli, Matteo Lisi, Hugo Rodriguez-Zanella, Sergio Kobal, Gergely Agoston, Albert Varga, Karina Wierzbowska-Drabik, Jarosław D Kasprzak, Rosina Arbucci, Olga Zhuravleva, J
pmc-11533336.description: ObjectiveAtrial cardiomyopathy is closely associated with atrial fibrillation (AF), and some patients exhibit no dysfunction at rest but demonstrate evident changes in left atrial (LA) function and LA volume during exercise. This study aimed to identify distinguishing signs during exercise stress echocardiography (ESE) among patients in sinus rhythm (SR), with and without history of paroxysmal/persistent AF (PAF).

pmc-13525698.title: Does radiographic imaging for spinal pain in patients receiving chiropractic care change patient outcomes? A pilot randomised controlled trial
pmc-13525698.creator: Hazel J. Jenkins, Mark Hancock, Aron Downie, Anika Young, Craig Moore, Stephney Whillier, Simon D. French
pmc-13525698.description: BackgroundImaging does not improve the management of non-specific spinal pain in randomised trials (RCTs) conducted in medical care settings. No RCTs have been performed to assess the benefit of imaging in chiropractic clinical settings, where it is postulated imaging may identify contraindications to, or inform application of, spinal manipulation.
